Declared tables
===============

A checked table keeps explicit IDs, row order and references in one data
declaration. Ordered views generate ordinary C. A project's checked-in
generated headers compile without Cesta; regeneration needs Cesta.

Commands
--------

  cesta tables check registry.data
  cesta tables rows registry.data Profiles id name
  cesta tables header registry.data -o registry_rows.h

check validates the complete bundle and prints it in normalized form. rows
prints a column projection without sorting, renumbering or deduplicating.
header writes one CESTA_TABLE_NAME_ROWS(row) X-macro per table. The supplied
row macro chooses how to use the fields.

Declaration
-----------

  (cesta-tables/1
    (Table Languages
      (Columns (Column code Identifier) (Column id Nat))
      (Key code) (Unique id)
      (Rows (Row he 0) (Row petta 2)))
    (Table Profiles
      (Columns (Column id Nat) (Column code Identifier)
               (Column language (Ref Languages code))
               (Column name Text) (Column enabled Bool)
               (Column feature (Enum always typing)))
      (Key id) (Unique code) (Unique language name)
      (Rows (Row 7 he_extended he "extended" true always)
            (Row 19 petta_extended petta "extended" false typing))))

Nat is a canonical decimal uint64 value. Identifier is an ASCII C identifier
spelling. Text is quoted. Bool is true or false. Enum admits only its listed
distinct identifier spellings. Ref carries the referenced scalar value; its
target must have a singleton primary key of a scalar type. Forward references
are allowed. Reference chains through key columns are refused.

Each table needs at least one column and a nonempty primary key. Keys may be
composite. Unique declarations add alternate keys. Rows must have exactly
the declared number of typed cells, keys must distinguish rows, and every
reference must find a target. (Dense id), when requested, requires a singleton
Nat primary key with IDs 0 through n-1 in the written row order. Sparse tables
do not acquire a dense profile. Unknown types, repeated schema sections,
duplicate keys and dangling references are refused with a reason.

C export
--------

A cesta-export/1 manifest can include:

  (table-enum "registry.data" Profiles
    (enum ProfileId) (prefix PROFILE_) (id id) (name code))
  (table-rows "registry.data" Profiles
    (macro TYPING_PROFILE_ROWS) (columns id code name)
    (where feature typing))
  (table-names "counters.data" Counters
    (array counter_names) (id id) (text spelling) (count COUNTER_COUNT))

table-enum needs Nat IDs representable by C11 int and C identifier suffixes.
Logical Identifier cells may spell keywords, but final exported declaration
names must avoid the shared C11/GNU keyword vocabulary. Thus a logical `if`
is allowed and exports as SAFE_if with a prefix; bare `if` is refused.
An optional count is the number of selected rows, not a bound on sparse IDs.
table-names needs a nonempty unfiltered Dense ID column, a Text column and the name
of the array bound. table-rows supports uint64 IDs without an int restriction.
An empty enum view requires a count enumerator; a bare empty enum and a
zero-length name array are refused. C declaration names must remain distinct
across the header, including enum constants, typedefs and its include guard.
Repeated where clauses are conjunctive. Filters preserve source order and
never renumber rows. Every requested column and filter type is checked even
when no rows match. A missing column is an error; a well-typed value absent
from a reference target may legitimately select an empty view.

All projection options are explicit. An option for a different projection
is refused. --plan records the normalized source bundle and each ordered
selected view. Identifier cells remain tokens; Nat cells use UINT64_C; Bool
cells use 0/1; string bytes use C escapes that cannot absorb following digits
or become trigraphs. The row macro's formal is fresh against emitted cells.
Callers remain responsible for declaring any identifier tokens they use.

Existing declarations
---------------------

The cesta-counters/1 format remains readable. Its dense-ID and uniqueness
checks use the shared table validator. Its fixed Counters embedding uses Nat,
Text and Text columns and preserves the original accepted suffix domain.
Operation contracts use the same validator for identities and resource,
charge and profile references. Their effect-specific laws remain separate.
Neither adapter imports another project's IDs or changes table order.

Evidence and boundaries
-----------------------

DeclaredTables proves check soundness/completeness for its typed data model,
unique keyed lookup, reference witnesses, and ordered filtered projections.
DeclaredCounterTables derives shared admission from ExportCounterTables.Dense
with the explicit uint64 row-count bound. Actual normalized source, views and
mutated records are checked by the Lean kernel in test-table-admission.
Large counter checks reuse chunked injective numeric-code evidence.

These are table and view laws. Native text parsing, C printing and compiler
behavior are tested boundaries. They do not prove arbitrary C handler effects
or the semantics of a project's registry lookup functions. Positive and
negative native fixtures run in test-tables; Lean checks stay in qualify.
